title: Nine hundred and fifty years
hook: Nuh calls his people by night and by day, openly and in private, and few listen (71:5–9; 29:14)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Habil, the brother who wouldn't raise his hand, and one life as all lives. Today, a man who kept talking for nine hundred and fifty years.
screen: `HABIL — ONE LIFE IS LIKE ALL LIVES.`

segments.voice: A teacher stands in front of a room where nobody's listening. Phones out, heads down, someone asleep in the back. She says it again, another way. Tries a joke. Tries a story. Stays after class in case anyone wants to ask. Almost nobody does. Now stretch that across many lifetimes. Nuh, Noah, is remembered for a boat. But the Qur'an spends whole passages on something else: how long he kept talking to people who wouldn't listen.
screen: `A ROOM WHERE NOBODY'S LISTENING.` → `SAY IT AGAIN, ANOTHER WAY.` → `NUH, BEFORE THE BOAT.`

segments.voice: A whole surah carries his name, surah seventy-one, and most of it is his own report to God. Paraphrasing: my Lord, I've called my people night and day, and my calling has only made them run further away. Every time I called them, so You could forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and pulled their clothes over their heads. I called them openly. I spoke to them in public, and I spoke to them in private. Night and day, loud and quiet, crowds and one at a time: he tried everything. And what was he asking? Not much: ask your Lord's forgiveness; He is forgiving. He promised them rain, and gardens, and rivers. Then the number. In Pickthall's words, “he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years.” Some scholars take it as it stands. Others note it describes how long he stayed among his people, and differ over how it fits his whole life. Either way, it's patience almost too long to imagine. And the result? The Qur'an is honest: only a few believed with him. By the world's measure, that looks like failure. But a hadith in Bukhari, about the Day of Judgment, has people coming to Nuh and calling him the first messenger to the people of the earth, and a grateful servant. His success wasn't counted in listeners. It was counted in the calling.
screen: `MY LORD, I'VE CALLED THEM NIGHT AND DAY.` · `FINGERS IN THEIR EARS.` · `A THOUSAND YEARS SAVE FIFTY.` · `ONLY A FEW BELIEVED.` · then, large: `CALL ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: Sit quietly and say, slowly, the words Nuh asked of his people: I ask God's forgiveness. Give each word its own breath, and repeat it a few times without hurrying. If you don't pray, let the words be a simple wish to begin again.
Nuh. Noah: the prophet who called his people night and day for nine hundred and fifty years, while only a few listened.
Your line: call anyway. Few listened, and he never stopped calling. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Nuh as a prophet, and surah seventy-one, which bears his name, is read as a lesson in patient, persistent calling.

options: give up; they've made their choice.

original.note: Arabic: "a thousand years less fifty," the Qur'an's way of saying nine hundred and fifty (29:14).

trapdoor: what you thought: Noah, the ark, the animals.
what it means: nine hundred and fifty years — how long Nuh called his people, every way he could, while few listened.

what a scholar hears: 29:14 says a thousand years less fifty; scholars differ over how it maps onto his whole life; and surah seventy-one gives his own report of calling by night and day, openly and in private.
recall: the last of the Qur'an's thirty parts

chat.says: If almost nobody listened to Nuh, was all his calling a failure?
options: No. A hadith calls him a grateful servant; his success was in the calling, not the crowd.
Yes, and it didn't help that he only ever preached in private, to his own family.
No, because in the end most of his people came round and believed with him.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an says only a few believed, yet a hadith calls Nuh a grateful servant. His success was counted in the calling.

Nuh.meaning: Noah, the prophet who called his people for 950 years

Pickthall.meaning: the English translator whose Qur'an wording this lesson quotes

Bukhari.meaning: Sahih al-Bukhari, the best-known collection of hadith

hadith.meaning: a report of what the Prophet ﷺ said or did

sources.quoted: he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years

sources.ref: Qur'an 71:5–12 (night and day; fingers in their ears; openly and in private; seek forgiveness)
Qur'an 11:40 (only a few believed with him)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4476 (the intercession: 'the first messenger to the people of the earth')

notes: Pickthall 29:14 quoted from memory ('And verily We sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers.'). Confirm.

950 years: many take it as the length of his mission among his people; some commentators report further years before or after. The script says 'scholars differ over how it fits his whole life'. Confirm.
Bukhari 4476 (intercession): Nuh called 'the first of the messengers to the people of the earth' and 'a grateful servant' (17:3). Confirm.
Original: alfa sanatin illa khamsina 'aman (29:14); the Arabic uses two different words for year (sana, 'am). Confirm the vowelling.
